rv.q: Lyndsey (a beautifully timed turn from Eliza Shea) is brighter than most and has ulterior motives, but tables are turned repeatedly in a tussle of one-upmanship and assertion of dominance in the second scene of John Donnelly's tautly written play.
The Pass successfully invites us right into the mind of Jason.

cn.t: This intimate pub theatre revival of Donnelly's football drama receives a mixed response, with critics finding the production intriguing in its exploration of sexuality in sports but ultimately uneven in execution.
